**<sub><sub>![P1 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P1-orange?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Ignore unreaped zombies when waiting for process-group shutdown**

In container environments whose PID 1 does not promptly reap orphaned grandchildren, `process.kill(-child.pid, 0)` continues succeeding after SIGKILL because the group contains only a zombie that this process cannot reap. This loop therefore always reaches the five-second error even though the descendant socket is already closed; fresh evidence from running the committed `scripts/material-facts-v7-http-process-tree.test.mjs` in the repository container is that all five lifecycle cases fail with `process group did not stop`, making the newly added mandatory `npm run check` suite fail. Detect live non-zombie members or verify the owned resources instead of requiring ESRCH.

AGENTS.md reference: [AGENTS.md:L7-L7](https://github.com/ZZZZihan/anxin-work-rights/blob/92ba4dd615eb3b5a43508902e3e217b96ea6df9c/AGENTS.md#L7-L7)

**<sub><sub>![P2 Badge](https://img.shields.io/badge/P2-yellow?style=flat)</sub></sub>  Verify the cancellation runner's whole process group stopped**

When a Wrangler descendant redirects its stdio and ignores SIGTERM, the parent can close and satisfy this await while that descendant remains alive; the SIGKILL branch is never entered, and this function clears `worker` without checking the detached process group. In the cancellation HTTP runner, which later restarts the Worker and eventually deletes its disposable state, that orphan can retain sockets or files and make the isolated regression flaky. Apply the group-liveness/KILL check used by the v7 runner before returning.
